summary: Margaret H. Dornish is a scholar in religious studies and Buddhist studies. She studied at Yale University, Claremont Graduate University, and the University of Southern California, and served as Associate Professor of Religion at Pomona College (attested 1989).

Margaret Mead (1901–1978) studied at DePauw, Barnard (BA), and Columbia (MA, PhD under Franz Boas). She held posts at the American Museum of Natural History (1926, 1946–1969), Columbia (1954–1978), Fordham (1968–1970), and Rhode Island (1970).

Margaret R. Miles (born 1937) works in religious studies and history/archaeology. She studied at San Francisco State University (BA) and Graduate Theological Union (PhD), and held posts at Harvard Divinity School (~1978–1996) and Graduate Theological Union (dean 1996–2001).

Margarita Angelica Delgado Creamer works in religious studies and Sinology. She completed her PhD at the University of Pittsburgh under doctoral supervisor Linda Penkower, and later studied under postdoctoral mentor Xiuping Hong.

Margarita Iosifovna Vorobyova-Desyatovskaya (1933–2021) was a Buddhist studies, Indology, and Iranian/Central Asian scholar. She studied at Saint Petersburg State University and the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts, serving at the Institute of Oriental Studies and as manuscript curator (1982–2005).
Margarita Kleibel is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied under MA supervisor Klaus-Dieter Mathes and teacher Karin Preisendanz.

Maria Heim works in Buddhist studies and Indology. She completed a BA at Reed College and a PhD at Harvard University under Charles Hallisey, serving as Associate Professor of Buddhist Studies at Amherst College (attested 2013–2020).

Marian Ury (1932–1995) was a scholar in Japanology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD from the University of California, Berkeley, and served as professor of East Asian languages and comparative literature at UC Davis from 1969 to 1995.

Marianne Pieper (born 1949) studied at Hamburger Hochschule für Wirtschaft und Politik and completed her Habilitation at Magdeburg (1996). She held appointments at the University of Kassel (1994–1996) and the University of Hamburg (1990–1994, and professor 1996–2015).

Marianne Winder (1918–2001) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of London, Nottingham, UCL, and SOAS under David Snellgrove, holding posts at Nottingham, University of London, and the Wellcome Trust (~1964–1978).

Marianne Yaldiz is a scholar of history, archaeology, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She served as Director at the Museum of Asian Art (attested 1997–2005) and Director at the Museum für Indische Kunst (attested 2006).
Marie G. Wanek is a scholar in Indology and philosophy. She studied at the University of Pennsylvania and studied under teacher Sengaku Mayeda.
Marie-Stella Boussemart studied under Samten Gyaltsen Karmay and Dagpo Rinpoche.

Marielle Harrison is a scholar in religious studies and Buddhist studies. She studied as a doctoral student at the University of Chicago and served as an HCBSS Postdoctoral Fellow Lecturer at Stanford University (attested 2026).
Marina Illich is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at Columbia University in 2006 under the supervision of Robert A. F. Thurman.

Mario D'Amato (born 1969) is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Chicago (~1994–2000) under Paul J. Griffiths, and held posts at Hampshire College (~2001–2006) and Rollins College (~2006).

Mario Poceski works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He completed his PhD at UCLA (2000) under Robert E. Buswell Jr., and held posts at the University of Iowa (2001) and the University of Florida (attested 2004–2019).

Mario Praz (1896–1982) studied at the University of Bologna (~1914–1918) and the University of Florence (~1918–1920). He held academic posts at the University of Manchester (~1932–1934) and Sapienza University of Rome (~1934–1966).
Marion L. Matics is a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies. Matics studied under doctoral supervisors Horace L. Friess and Royal W. Weiler, as well as under teacher Robert A. Fowkes.

Marion Meyer (born 1954) is a scholar in history and archaeology. She held posts at the German Archaeological Institute (1984–1985), the University of Florida (1996), the University of Bonn (~1997–2003), and the University of Vienna (~2003–2020).
